title: Devin AI Pricing 2026: Plans and Real Cost per Task
summary: Devin AI pricing includes a $0 to $200 base fee plus metered compute unit costs.
body_markdown:
## Connect Devin to ticket and alert workflows with Activepieces


The cheapest task is the one you never start, and Activepieces can decide what reaches Devin and where the result goes, at 1 credit a run however many steps the flow has.


Once you've stopped delegating a type of work, the same logic applies upstream: stop sending Devin tickets that were never ready.


### Filter tickets before they reach Devin


Every session Devin starts burns compute units, and a vague ticket is the surest way to burn them on work that gets rejected.


Activepieces sits between your sources and Devin. A trigger fires when a ticket is created in your tracker or an alert arrives from your monitoring feed, and a filter step then checks what came in.


The MIT-licensed core carries 746 integrations, counted from the open source monorepo under packages/integrations/community, and roughly 60% of them are community-contributed, so a tracker or monitoring feed is likely already a integration in that folder.


The integration action that runs as a step in your flow is the same one exposed as a tool on the project's MCP server, as the Integrations Framework and MCP Server documentation describe.


The filter is where the money is saved. Drop tickets with no reproduction steps, no acceptance criteria, or no linked repository, and you've removed the sessions most likely to cost units and produce nothing mergeable.


Tickets that pass go on to start a Devin session with the full ticket text as the prompt. Rejected ones can go back to the author with a request for detail, which costs you a message instead of a session.


The flow below shows the path. Tracker and alert feed in on the left, the filter discards vague items, clear ones pass to Devin, and the result card goes out to[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) and the tracker.


*(illustration)*


Read it as a gate placed before the meter starts running. Whatever the filter rejects never reaches Devin's billing at all.


### Post results back to the team


When a Devin session finishes, a final step formats a result card: what was attempted, the pull request link, and whether the session ended in success or a stall.


Activepieces posts that card to a Slack channel and writes it back to the originating ticket, so the person who owns the work sees the outcome where they already look, and with 746 integrations in the open source monorepo that is two steps in one flow, not two systems.


That record is also what makes cost per merged task measurable. If every result lands on the ticket, you can count which tasks merged and which ended in rework, then divide your unit spend accordingly.


On price, Activepieces bills separately from Devin: the Free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month, and Plus is $20 a month for 10,000 credits, then $0.007 a credit over. The full list is on its[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) . Devin's bill is unaffected by it.


Before building anything, check whether Devin's native integrations already cover your tracker and Slack. If they do, you may only need Activepieces for the filter, and its MIT-licensed core can run on your own infrastructure if tickets can't leave it.
